title: The Missing Alibi
premise: Ivo Dravenmoor, a night-shift taxi dispatcher with a gift for noticing what others miss, has quietly untangled three deaths the police ruled accidental. When a drowned woman washes up at Greywater Point wearing clothes stolen from Ivo's own closet, the killer makes it personal — someone is staging murders from inside Ivo's life, using dispatch logs and case knowledge only an insider could possess. As Ivo investigates alongside Detective Maren Kolvek, who suspects Ivo herself, they uncover a decades-old inheritance scheme tied to the Dravenmoor family estate and a love affair that duty forced apart. The killer is Ivo's estranged half-brother, Silas, who believes the inheritance was stolen from him and has been rehearsing his revenge on the one person who might have understood him. In the climax at the tide flats, Ivo offers Silas the belonging he's always wanted instead of a fight, and Silas surrenders as the water gives up its final secret: a letter proving their mother loved them both.
about_author: Astrid Thornbury spent a decade answering phones for a coastal cab company before turning her ear for late-night confessions into fiction. She writes mysteries about ordinary people who notice too much, from a house above the tide flats.

chapters.title: The Night Frequency
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A slow night shift establishes Ivo's world: the dispatch board, the drivers' voices, the habit of listening between the lines. A call comes in about a body at Greywater Point, and Ivo recognizes the address from a pattern she's been quietly tracking across three 'accidents.' Emotional beat: restless vigilance hardening into dread.

chapters.title: Clothes That Weren't Hers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the seawall, police hold back a crowd while the dead woman is pulled from the shallows — wearing Ivo's own missing cardigan and scarf. Detective Maren Kolvek arrives and fixes on Ivo immediately. Flashback threads reveal Ivo's three prior quiet investigations. Emotional beat: violation; the case has stepped inside her skin.

chapters.title: What the Log Knows
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with a brief Kolvek interlude. Ivo audits her own dispatch logs and finds calls placed in her voice-print window that she never made — someone with system access. Kolvek interviews her, alternating suspicion and reluctant respect. Emotional beat: paranoia blooming; home no longer feels safe.

chapters.title: The House Above the Flats
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo returns to the shuttered Dravenmoor family house to search her late mother's papers and finds a second name on old documents: Silas. Her aunt lets slip that Mother had a son given up long before Ivo was born. Emotional beat: grief cracking open into a hunger for the truth about her family.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Hand
chapters.summary: Kolvek's POV. Kolvek reopens the three prior deaths and finds each victim connected to the Dravenmoor estate's trustees — and each file annotated by an unseen hand with corrections no outsider could know. She begins to believe Ivo is a target, not a suspect. Emotional beat: grudging alliance forming under professional doubt.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Hidden in her mother's writing desk, Ivo finds unsent letters addressed to Silas — love tangled with duty, a child surrendered to protect an inheritance. The fourth letter names the tide flats and a meeting that never happened. Emotional beat: tenderness and fury; understanding the wound that made the killer.

chapters.title: The Man Who Answers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Using the dispatch board, Ivo traces the phantom calls to a payphone route and coaxes the caller into conversation, recognizing Silas's cadence — he's been listening to her nights for months. He quotes her mother's letters back to her. Emotional beat: horrified intimacy; the killer knows her better than anyone alive.

chapters.title: Trustee's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Kolvek's POV. The last surviving trustee is found drugged but alive, and his testimony exposes how the estate was legally strangled away from Silas decades ago. Kolvek realizes the killings follow the order of the original betrayal — and that Ivo is last on the list. Emotional beat: urgency compressing into a race against the tide tables.

chapters.title: Greywater Point, Low Tide
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Luring Silas with the fourth letter, Ivo meets him alone on the flats as the water turns. He wants her to choose: condemn the family or join him in erasing it. Instead she offers him what he actually lost — acknowledgment, a place, her name spoken beside his. Emotional beat: love against duty, offered at knife-point.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Ivo and Kolvek POVs interleaved. Silas wavers as sirens cross the causeway; when he nearly drowns reaching for the final letter the sea uncovered, Ivo pulls him out, and he surrenders. Weeks later, Ivo visits him in custody and reads their mother's words aloud. Emotional beat: sorrowful peace; belonging built rather than inherited.
